newsitem.title: UK: Details of UK wool sale - for January 8.
newsitem.headline: Details of UK wool sale - for January 8.

text.p: Wednesday's official sale of Scottish raw wool saw prices fall by an average of four pence with Halfbreds alone in bullish mood, according to information supplied by the British Wool Marketing Board.
Crosses lost between four and six pence per kg in limited post-holiday business and Blackface prices fell by up to six pence since the last Scottish sale on November 13.
The market indicator dropped three points since the previous Scottish sale on November 13, taking it to the season's low of 103.
Among the Halfbreds, Scottish descriptions sold for 115-118 pence per kg, gaining up to two pence per kg but Northern Ireland origins were quoted down by up to six pence at 95-96 pence per kg.
Other wools from Northern Ireland lost four pence per kg, with Crosses selling for around 110 pence and Blackfaces going for 108.
An offering of Swaledales also sold for around two pence below prices achieved at the last UK auction on December 11.
Carpet-friendly Swaledale Greys were quoted at 86.5 to 87.5 pence per kg.
Spot wools accounted for 1.49 million of the total 2.189 million kg offering.
The 708,000 kg forward wools on offer included 170,000 kg of the next season's clip but only just under half was sold in a slow resumption of trade.
The overall clearance rate for Wednesday's sale stood at 76 percent.
